newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt share prices streak to 14th record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt share prices streak to 14th record high.

text.p: The all-share index on the Cairo stock exchange added to a two-week long run on Wednesday amid high turnover in Pyramids Breweries shares.
The index rose 1.27 percent to close at 399.6 points, or 5.0 points from 394.6 points on Tuesday, the Capital Markets Authority said.
It is the 14th record high for the index in as many days.
Turnover was 98.82 million pounds ($29.06 million). One broker said volume was swollen by high trade in Pyramids, also known as Al-Ahram Beverages.
"Forty-two million of the turnover was in Al-Ahram Beverages," said broker Dalia Sultan of EFG Hermes.
Its share closed up 4.74 pounds at 99.67.
The Egyptian state had said in November that it sold 74.9 percent of its share in the brewery to six international funds in a deal worth 231 million pounds.
"It might have been they (the new buyers) were reselling to the public," said Sultan. "Otherwise it was just a normal day with most of the milling shares going up again."

Commercial International Bank closed steady at 630 pounds. The price had risen 30 pounds on Tuesday, when banks were the best performing sector. "CIB is still trading at 630 because no one wants to sell at this price," Sultan said.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 662.44 points from 651.87 on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 264.43 from 261.75 points.
Out of the 78 shares traded, 47 gained, 11 lost and 20 ended the day unchanged.
